questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the simple present tense?

options.a: She walks to school every day.
options.d: She will walk to school tomorrow.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is in the simple past tense?

options.a: She visited her grandmother last week.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the future tense?

options.a: She will travel to London next month.
options.c: She is travelling to London now.
options.d: She travelled to London last year.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct present perfect sentence.

options.a: I have lived here for five years.
options.b: I live here for five years.
options.c: I lived here for five years.
options.d: I am living here for five years.

questions.explanation: 'have lived' = present perfect (action from past to present).

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the past perfect tense?

options.a: She had finished her homework before dinner.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'can' correctly?

options.b: I can to speak three languages.
options.d: I am can speak three languages.

questions.explanation: 'can' + base verb = ability (no 'to', no -s, no 'am can').

questions.questionText: Identify the sentence using 'must' for obligation.

options.a: You must wear a helmet when cycling.
options.b: You must to wear a helmet.
options.d: You are must wear a helmet.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'should' correctly?

options.a: You should study harder for the exam.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'may' for permission?

options.a: May I go to the toilet, please?
options.b: I may to go to the toilet.
options.c: I am may go to the toilet.
options.d: I cans go to the toilet.

questions.questionText: Identify the first conditional sentence.

options.a: If it rains, I will stay at home.
options.b: If it rained, I would stay at home.
options.c: If it had rained, I would have stayed home.
options.d: If it rains, I stay at home.

questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present, will + base verb (real future possibility).

questions.questionText: Identify the second conditional sentence.

options.a: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
options.b: If I win the lottery, I will travel the world.
options.c: If I had won the lottery, I would have traveled.

questions.explanation: Second conditional: If + past, would + base verb (hypothetical present/future).

questions.questionText: Identify the third conditional sentence.

options.a: If I had studied harder, I would have passed.
options.b: If I study harder, I will pass.
options.c: If I studied harder, I would pass.

questions.explanation: Third conditional: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle (past hypothetical).

questions.questionText: Identify the zero conditional sentence.

options.a: If you heat water to 100°C, it boils.
options.b: If it rains tomorrow, I will stay home.
options.c: If I had money, I would travel.
options.d: If you study, you will pass.

questions.explanation: Zero conditional: If + present simple, present simple (general truth).

questions.questionText: Change to passive: 'She writes a letter.'

options.a: A letter is written by her.
options.b: A letter is wrote by her.
options.d: A letter being written by her.

questions.explanation: Passive present simple: am/is/are + past participle.

questions.questionText: Change to passive: 'They built the house.'

options.a: The house was built by them.
options.b: The house is built by them.
options.d: The house were built by them.

questions.explanation: Passive past simple: was/were + past participle.

questions.questionText: Change to passive: 'The cat chased the mouse.'

options.a: The mouse was chased by the cat.
options.b: The mouse is chased by the cat.
options.c: The mouse chased by the cat.
options.d: The cat was chased by the mouse.

questions.explanation: Passive: subject becomes agent after 'by', object becomes new subject.

questions.questionText: Convert to reported speech: 'She is a doctor,' Tom said.

options.a: Tom said that she was a doctor.
options.b: Tom said that she is a doctor.
options.c: Tom told that she was a doctor.
options.d: Tom said I was a doctor.

questions.explanation: Reported speech: present tense → past tense (is → was).

questions.questionText: Transform to reported speech: 'What time is it?' he asked.

options.a: He asked what time it was.
options.b: He asked what time is it.
options.c: He asked what time it is.
options.d: He asked what time did it be.

questions.explanation: Reported question: statement form + tense backshift.

questions.questionText: Convert to reported speech: 'Close the door,' she said.

options.a: She told me to close the door.
options.c: She said to close the door.
options.d: She said that close the door.

questions.explanation: Reported command: told + person + to + base verb.

Choose the correct sentence with article 'an'.
Choose the correct sentence with article 'the'.

options.a: The sun rises in the east.
options.b: A sun rises in a east.

options.a: The teacher who taught us is kind.

options.a: The car which I bought is blue.

questions.questionText: Choose the synonym of 'happy'.
Choose the antonym of 'happy'.
What does the idiom 'break the ice' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Break the ice' = initiate conversation in awkward situation.

questions.questionText: What does 'take off' mean in 'The plane took off'?
questions.explanation: 'Take off' (aviation) = depart the ground / become airborne.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct collocation.
Identify the compound word.
What does the prefix 'un-' mean in 'unhappy'?
What does the suffix '-able' mean in 'readable'?
Identify the noun formed from the verb 'to educate'.
Identify the adjective formed from the noun 'danger'.
Identify the homophone pair.
Identify a word with multiple meanings (polysemy).
Which word would appear first in a dictionary?
In 'The arid desert has no water', the word 'arid' means?
What does 'analyze' mean in academic context?
Read: 'The rain forests are being cut down at an alarming rate. Many animals lose their homes. We must act now.' What is the main idea?

options.a: Rain forests are being destroyed and we must protect them.

questions.explanation: Main idea = rain forest destruction + need for protection.

questions.questionText: Read: 'Sarah bought three apples and two oranges at the market yesterday.' How many apples did Sarah buy?
Read: 'Tom looked at the dark clouds and sighed.' How did Tom feel?
Read: 'First, she woke up. Then, she brushed her teeth. Finally, she ate breakfast.' What happened first?
Read: 'It rained heavily, so the roads were flooded.' What is the cause?
Read: 'Unlike her sister who loves mathematics, Maria prefers literature.' Who loves mathematics?
Read: 'The puppy was so tiny it fit in my palm.' What does 'palm' refer to?
questions.explanation: Context clue 'puppy fit in my palm' = inner hand.

questions.questionText: Read: 'Tom told Jack that he was late.' Who is 'he'?
questions.explanation: Pronoun reference: 'he' is ambiguous in this sentence.

questions.questionText: Read: 'What a disaster! This is the worst day ever!' What is the tone?
Read: 'You should always wash your hands before eating. This prevents germs from spreading.' What is the author's purpose?
questions.explanation: Author's purpose: advise ('you should') + inform ('prevents germs').

questions.questionText: Read passage about recycling benefits. Which is the best summary?
questions.explanation: Summary captures main idea: recycling = environmental benefit.

questions.questionText: Read: 'The boy kept eating junk food every day.' What will likely happen?
questions.explanation: Prediction: continuous junk food → health problems.

questions.questionText: Read: 'Mary always helped her friends. She shared her food and listened to their problems.' What kind of person is Mary?
questions.explanation: Character inference: helped + shared + listened = kind/helpful.

questions.questionText: Read: 'The library opens at 9 AM and closes at 6 PM. It is closed on Sundays.' When is the library open?
questions.explanation: Factual recall: 9 AM to 6 PM, closed Sundays.

questions.questionText: Read: 'While Anna enjoys reading, her brother prefers sports.' What is the contrast?

options.a: Anna reads vs brother plays sports.

questions.questionText: Identify the declarative sentence.
Identify the interrogative sentence.

Identify the exclamatory sentence.
Identify the simple sentence.

options.c: She sings when she is happy.

questions.questionText: Identify the compound sentence.

options.b: I came because I wanted to see.

questions.explanation: Compound: two independent clauses joined by 'and'.

questions.questionText: Identify the complex sentence.

options.a: I left because I was tired.
options.b: I left and I was tired.

questions.explanation: Complex: independent + dependent ('because I was tired').

questions.questionText: Identify the compound-complex sentence.

options.a: When I arrived, he left and she stayed.

questions.explanation: Active past: subject + past tense + object.

questions.questionText: Combine: 'She is tired. She continues working.'

options.c: She is tired but working continues.

questions.questionText: Choose the formal apology.

options.a: I sincerely apologize for the inconvenience.

questions.explanation: Formal apology: 'I sincerely apologize for the inconvenience.'

questions.questionText: Choose the formal thank you.

questions.questionText: Choose the polite request.
questions.explanation: Polite request: 'Could you please help me?'

options.a: I wish to lodge a formal complaint regarding...

questions.questionText: At a restaurant, what would you say to order?

options.a: Could I have the menu, please?

questions.explanation: Restaurant: 'Could I have the menu, please?' = polite request.

questions.questionText: What would you say to ask for a price?
questions.explanation: Shopping: 'How much does this cost?' = asking price.

questions.questionText: How would you ask to borrow a pen from classmate?

options.a: Could I borrow your pen, please?

questions.explanation: School: 'Could I borrow your pen, please?' = polite.

questions.questionText: At airport, what would you ask?
questions.explanation: Travel: 'Where is the check-in counter?' = asking direction.

questions.questionText: What would you say to a doctor about symptoms?

options.a: I have been having a headache.

questions.explanation: Doctor: 'I have been having a headache' = describing symptoms.

questions.questionText: When answering phone, what do you say first?
How do you ask for direction politely?

options.a: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to...?

questions.explanation: Direction: 'Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to...?'

questions.questionText: What would you say when booking a hotel?

options.a: I'd like to book a room for two nights.

questions.explanation: Hotel: 'I'd like to book a room for two nights.'

questions.questionText: What would you say when introducing yourself in an interview?

options.a: Good morning, my name is... and I am here for... interview.

questions.questionText: How do you apologize for missing a deadline?

options.a: I apologize for missing the deadline.

questions.explanation: Apology: 'I apologize for missing the deadline.'

questions.questionText: Read: 'The rose blooms in the garden.' What imagery is used?
questions.explanation: Imagery: 'rose blooms' = visual image of flower.

questions.questionText: Read: 'The cat sat on the mat / The dog ran very fast / I went to bed / And dreamed in my head.' What is the rhyme scheme?
questions.explanation: Lines rhyme: 'mat/fast' (A) 'bed/head' (B), wait — line 3 'bed' doesn't rhyme with line 1 'mat' or line 2 'fast'. Line 4 'head' rhymes with line 3 'bed'. So AABB? Actually 'mat/fast' don't rhyme (mat/fast are different). Re-check.

questions.questionText: Read: 'Her voice is music to my ears.' What is the figurative language?
Read: 'How lovely is the morning sun! / It shines on everyone.' What is the speaker's tone?
Read: 'Time waits for no one / It flies like a bird / We must use it well.' What is the theme?
questions.explanation: Theme: time is precious and must be used wisely.
